description: Index of App-manifest validation fixtures. Each entry points at a case file; the CASE FILE is the single source of truth for that case's expected outcome, and this index deliberately does not repeat it. A runner enumerates 'cases', loads each file, and reads expectedOutcome and enforcedBy from the file itself.

caseFileShape.caseId: stable identifier, referenced in QA reports
caseFileShape.kind: 'manifest' — the case carries a whole App manifest to validate | 'invocation' — the case describes a call against an already-validated manifest
caseFileShape.title: one line, what the case is
caseFileShape.coversRequirement: which stated AZ7 requirement this case covers, or 'none' for undecided cases
caseFileShape.enforcedBy: 'schema' — decidable by app-manifest.schema.json alone | 'validator' — referential, NOT expressible in JSON Schema, owed by the registry-aware validator | 'schema+validator' — both layers must agree | 'runtime' — an invocation-time obligation, not decidable from any manifest | 'undecided'
caseFileShape.why: why this outcome is required, in security terms
caseFileShape.notes: the schema-versus-validator split for this case, and any trap in reading its result
caseFileShape.manifest: present when kind is 'manifest' — the App manifest under test
caseFileShape.invocation: present when kind is 'invocation' — the declaring case, the authenticated context, the client-supplied request, the attack, and the required outcome

sets.subject: AZ7 — an own-scope Action must name the Entity it operates on, and that Entity must itself carry the ownership relation.

pairsThatMustBeReportedTogether.reason: Structurally identical apart from which entity the own-scope Action targets. n4 must be REJECTED and p2 must be ACCEPTED. Both rejected means the validator bans unowned entities instead of enforcing AZ7; both accepted means AZ7 is not implemented and CWE-863 is still open.
The same empty entities array, with and without an own-scope Action. Proves the rejection in n6 comes from 'own' and not from emptiness.

An unresolvable reference, and an unresolvable reference that differs only by case. Both must be REJECTED. Accepting n5d means reference resolution was made case-insensitive to fix n2, which is itself a bypass.

sets.excludedFromTotalsHistory: az7-q1 and az7-q2 were authored as UNDECIDED open questions and excluded from totals. Both were subsequently decided by AUTHORIZATION_STANDARD.md §4.1 VALIDATOR-AZ7 — item 5 for az7-q1, item 3 for az7-q2 — and now carry expectedOutcome REJECT at the validator layer. Their case files keep the provenance.
